title: Effectiveness of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Preventing Semantic NetOps Violations — Repaired Preregistration
research_question: Does deterministic verification plus bounded LLM-guided repair (GVR) reduce verifier-detected semantic invariant violations (reachability or policy/ACL breaches) relative to (A) unconstrained LLM generation and (B) schema-constrained decoding alone on a public synthetic NetOps task bank?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: The GVR arm (C) has a lower proportion of verifier-detected semantic invariant violations than unconstrained LLM generation (A) on paired tasks.
H2: The GVR arm (C) has a lower proportion of verifier-detected semantic invariant violations than schema-constrained decoding (B) on paired tasks.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: How does repair-iteration count correlate with topology size and policy complexity?
EQ2: What semantic failure modes remain after GVR (category tallies from deterministic diagnostics)?
benchmark_scope: Public synthetic NetOps task bank v1 (released subset): 12 topology/policy clusters × 20 tasks each = 240 tasks; each task = intent + reference topology + policy predicates. (See dataset-generation procedure; license: permissive public dataset release.)
primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (proportion of tasks with verifier-detected semantic violations; estimand computed as paired difference: rate(C) - rate(baseline) using paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor).
secondary_estimands: Absolute risk reduction (C vs A and C vs B) with 95% Wilson CIs.
Distribution of repair iterations until verifier acceptance (empirical survival function).
Logistic regression coefficients for topology_size and policy_complexity as moderators of GVR effectiveness (exploratory).
sampling_plan: Confirmatory sample: N = 240 tasks as a single paired experiment per adapter run. Structure: 12 topology/policy clusters × 20 tasks per cluster = 240 tasks. For each task the adapter produces paired outputs for baseline and guarded conditions (one primary generated configuration per condition). Confirmatory primary analysis compares guarded vs baseline in a paired manner. To address the two prespecified primary comparisons (H1 and H2), the study will execute two adapter-configured paired experiments (same task set, same RNG seeds, separate adapter baseline parameterization): (i) baseline parameterized as unconstrained generation (test H1), (ii) baseline parameterized as schema-constrained decoding (test H2). Each adapter-configured paired experiment uses the same preregistered sampling script and RNG seed set; each experiment has task_count = 240. All scripts, RNG seeds, and deterministic sampling procedures are archived prior to execution.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Target effect: absolute reduction of 10 percentage points (e.g., baseline violation rate 20% → target 10% in GVR arm). With N=240 paired tasks and paired-analysis heuristics (paired McNemar-like), power >80% for an approximate 10 percentage-point paired reduction under plausible discordance assumptions. Exact pre-execution power calculations will be run by the registered analysis executor and archived. Sensitivity power recalculations will be performed for baseline rates 10% and 30% and for alternative within-pair correlation assumptions.
exclusion_rules: Pairs with irrecoverable infrastructure/model-call failures are handled per analysis executor 'complete_pair_primary' rules (documented in execution manifest).

Repair attempts that exceed the allowed edit budget are not counted as successful repairs and are tallied separately; such pairs remain in the dataset but flagged and included in conservative sensitivity analyses.
missingness_plan: API/infra failures or timeouts during a pair are recorded in the execution manifest. Primary analysis follows the registered executor's 'complete_pair_primary' handling: pairs with irrecoverable infrastructure/model-call failures are excluded from the paired test only when exclusion criteria per executor are met; otherwise the executor's rules determine inclusion. A sensitivity analysis ('complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity') will treat failed/missing model-call outputs as semantic-violation positives (conservative). Verifier timeouts are flagged and placed into sensitivity analyses (conservative treatment as violation unless golden-reference indicates otherwise).
analysis_plan: Primary comparisons: (C vs A) and (C vs B), executed as two adapter-configured paired experiments (same task set). Use the registered analysis executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' (primary_estimand_id). Primary test: paired McNemar-style exact test implemented by the executor; compute absolute risk reduction and 95% Wilson CIs. Multiple-comparison correction: Bonferroni across the two prespecified primary comparisons (alpha_family = 0.05 → per-comparison alpha = 0.025). Report unadjusted p-values and corrected decision. Primary failed-call treatment: 'complete_pair_primary'; sensitivity analysis: 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity'. Exploratory analyses: logistic regression for moderators, iteration-to-acceptance survival summaries, and failure-mode tallies. All exploratory tests are labeled and interpreted as exploratory.
multiplicity_plan: Two prespecified primary comparisons (C vs A, C vs B). Apply Bonferroni correction (per-comparison alpha = 0.025). Unadjusted p-values provided for transparency; all other tests are exploratory and reported as such.

stopping_rule: Fixed-N confirmatory design: do not stop early for efficacy. Full preregistered execution of N=240 tasks per adapter-configured paired experiment is required. Technical restarts for infrastructure failures are permitted only to recover from genuine infra errors and must be logged; scientific reruns to change outcomes are prohibited.
planned_outputs: Raw generated configurations (all arms, all calls).
Verifier diagnostics (structured) for every generated artifact.
Analysis outputs: paired tests, CIs, logistic regressions, failure-mode tallies.
